def: In a way that suits the situation; for that reason.
以符合情況的方式；因此。
ex: The deadline has moved, so please adjust your schedule accordingly.
截止日期已經改了，所以請相應調整你的時程。
The forecast calls for heavy rain, so dress accordingly when you visit the site.
預報會下大雨，所以到現場參觀時請穿著合宜。
The contract was never signed. Accordingly, the supplier has no duty to deliver.
合約從未簽署，因此供應商沒有交貨的義務。
We expected higher demand in December and have staffed the store accordingly.
我們預期十二月需求較高，並已據此安排門市人力。
Please inform your team of the new policy so they can act accordingly.
請告知你的團隊新政策，讓他們能據此行事。

note: Links a reason to a result; accordingly can also mean in the way the situation requires.
連接原因與結果；accordingly 還能表示「依情況所需的方式」。
Stresses a direct result of something that just happened; slightly more formal.
強調前面事情直接造成的結果；稍微更正式。
A preposition phrase meaning as stated by; accordingly stands alone and means therefore or appropriately.
介系詞片語，意為「依…所說」；accordingly 可單獨使用，意為「因此」或「適當地」。

def: An official check of financial records or procedures; to carry out such a check.
對財務紀錄或作業程序所做的正式查核；進行這類查核。
ex: The accounting firm will conduct an annual audit of our books in March.
會計師事務所將在三月對我們的帳冊進行年度審計。
Tax officials audited the company's returns for the past three years.
稅務人員查核了這家公司過去三年的報稅資料。
An internal audit found that several safety inspections had not been recorded.
一項內部稽核發現有幾次安全檢查沒有留下紀錄。
Suppliers must pass a quality audit before we sign a long-term contract.
供應商必須通過品質稽核，我們才會簽長期合約。
The bank will audit all of its branches for compliance next quarter.
銀行下一季將稽核所有分行的法規遵循情況。

note: A general check of something, often physical; an audit usually examines records and systems against a standard.
泛指對事物的檢查，常是實體檢查；audit 通常是對照標準查核紀錄與制度。
A looser, less formal look at how something is going; an audit is official and systematic.
較不正式的檢討；audit 則是正式且有系統的查核。
An auditorium is a large hall for an audience; it is not related to checking accounts.
auditorium 是容納觀眾的大禮堂，與查帳無關。

def: A machine that makes copies of documents.
用來複印文件的機器。
ex: The copier on the third floor is out of paper again.
三樓的影印機又沒紙了。
Please call the technician; the copier keeps jamming.
請叫技術人員來；影印機一直卡紙。
We leased a new color copier instead of buying one.
我們租了一台新的彩色影印機，而不是買一台。
She left the original on the copier glass by mistake.
她不小心把原稿留在影印機的玻璃面板上。
Each department shares one copier, so print only what you need.
每個部門共用一台影印機，所以只印你需要的份量。

note: Same machine; copy machine is the plain everyday phrase, and copier is the shorter form.
同一種機器；copy machine 是平實的日常說法，copier 是較簡短的說法。
Same machine; used more in British English, while Americans usually say copier or copy machine.
同一種機器；較常見於英式英語，美國人通常說 copier 或 copy machine。
A printer prints documents sent from a computer; a copier duplicates paper originals, though many machines do both.
printer 列印電腦傳來的檔案；copier 複印紙本原稿，不過許多機器兩者兼具。

zh: 版權、著作權；為…取得版權
def: The legal right to control the copying and use of an original work.
控制原創作品被複製與使用的法定權利。
ex: The photographer holds the copyright to every image on the website.
這位攝影師擁有網站上每一張圖片的版權。
Copying the report without permission may violate copyright law.
未經許可複製這份報告可能違反著作權法。
The design firm copyrighted its icon collection before putting it online.
這家設計公司在把圖示集上線前先登記了版權。
The film studio sued the website for copyright infringement.
電影公司以侵害著作權為由控告該網站。
The copyright on this manual belongs to the manufacturer, not to us.
這本手冊的版權屬於製造商，不屬於我們。

note: A patent protects an invention or a technical method; copyright protects original writing, art, music or software code.
patent 保護發明或技術方法；copyright 保護原創的文字、藝術、音樂或程式碼。
A trademark protects a name or symbol that identifies a business; copyright protects creative works.
trademark 保護識別企業的名稱或標誌；copyright 保護創作作品。

def: Having a fault, so that something does not work or was not made correctly.
有缺陷，以致無法正常運作或製作不當。
ex: We will replace any defective product within thirty days of purchase.
購買後三十天內，我們會更換任何有瑕疵的產品。
A defective battery forced the manufacturer to recall thousands of laptops.
一顆有瑕疵的電池迫使製造商召回數千台筆記型電腦。
The customer returned the toaster because its heating element was defective.
顧客退回了烤麵包機，因為加熱元件有瑕疵。
Inspectors rejected the batch after finding that ten percent of the units were defective.
檢驗人員發現百分之十的成品有瑕疵後，拒收了整批貨。
The contract lets the buyer return defective goods for a full refund.
合約允許買方退回有瑕疵的貨品並取得全額退款。

note: More common in everyday speech; defective often points to a flaw from manufacturing.
較常用於日常口語；defective 常指製造時就有的缺陷。
Used for plans, arguments and designs as well as objects; defective is mainly for products.
也可用於計畫、論點與設計；defective 主要用於產品。
Deficient means lacking something needed, such as quality or quantity; defective means broken or badly made.
deficient 指缺少所需的東西，如品質或數量；defective 指壞掉或做得不好。

def: To move people out of a place because it is dangerous.
因為有危險而讓人撤離某個地方。
ex: Staff were told to evacuate the building when the fire alarm sounded.
火警響起時，員工被告知要撤離大樓。
Hotel managers evacuated the guests to a nearby conference center during the gas leak.
瓦斯外洩期間，飯店經理把住客疏散到附近的會議中心。
Residents were ordered to evacuate before the typhoon reached the coast.
颱風登陸海岸前，居民被命令撤離。
Everyone must evacuate the floor calmly and use the stairs, not the elevators.
大家必須冷靜地撤離樓層，走樓梯，不要搭電梯。
The airline had to evacuate the terminal after a security threat.
接獲安全威脅後，航空公司必須疏散航廈內的人員。

note: Plain, everyday word (clear the room); evacuate suggests an organized exit in an emergency.
平實的日常用語（clear the room）；evacuate 暗示緊急狀況下有組織的撤離。
To leave a room, seat or property you were using; there need not be any danger involved.
指離開你原本使用的房間、座位或房產；不一定與危險有關。

def: Something that can cause harm or danger.
可能造成傷害或危險的事物。
ex: Loose cables are a trip hazard, so please tape them down.
鬆脫的電線容易絆倒人，所以請用膠帶固定。
The inspector listed several fire hazards in the warehouse.
檢查人員列出倉庫內幾項火災隱患。
Employees should report any hazard to their supervisor immediately.
員工應立即向主管回報任何危險。
Wet floors in the kitchen are a serious safety hazard.
廚房濕滑的地板是嚴重的安全隱患。
I won't hazard a guess about next year's sales figures.
對於明年的銷售數字，我不敢貿然猜測。

note: General word for possible harm anywhere; a hazard is a specific source of harm, often in safety rules.
泛指任何可能的傷害；hazard 是具體的危險來源，常見於安全規定。
Risk is the chance that harm will happen; a hazard is the thing that could cause it.
risk 是傷害發生的可能性；hazard 是可能造成傷害的事物。
Haphazard means done without order or planning; it describes how something is done, not a danger.
haphazard 指毫無條理或計畫地進行，描述做事方式，而非危險。

def: To ask for information about something.
詢問某事的資訊。
ex: I am writing to inquire about the availability of conference rooms in May.
我來信是想詢問五月是否還有會議室可用。
Several customers have inquired whether the store will extend its hours.
有幾位顧客詢問過本店是否會延長營業時間。
Please inquire at the front desk if you need a late checkout.
如需延後退房，請洽櫃檯詢問。
The auditors will inquire into the reasons for the delay.
稽核人員將調查延誤的原因。
He called the agency to inquire how much a corporate package would cost.
他打電話給旅行社，詢問企業方案的價格。

note: Everyday word; inquire is more formal and typical of letters, emails and official situations.
日常用語；inquire 較正式，常見於信件、電子郵件與官方場合。
To question whether something is correct or to put a question to an authority; often about a detail.
指質疑某事是否正確，或向主管單位提問；常針對細節。
To request is to ask for something to be given or done; to inquire is to ask for information.
request 是要求給予某物或做某事；inquire 是詢問資訊。

def: To get in the way of something, or to become involved in what is not your business.
妨礙某事，或介入與自己無關的事。
ex: Construction noise should not interfere with the morning meetings.
施工噪音不應該干擾早上的會議。
Our manager rarely interferes in how the teams organize their own tasks.
我們經理很少干涉各團隊如何安排自己的工作。
Heavy traffic interfered with the delivery schedule all week.
壅塞的車流整個星期都影響到配送時程。
Strong winds interfered with the signal, and the video call dropped.
強風干擾了訊號，視訊通話就斷了。
Please do not interfere with the equipment; call maintenance instead.
請不要擅動設備；改叫維修人員來處理。

note: To break up a process or event so that it cannot continue normally; interfere with can be milder.
使流程或活動無法正常進行；interfere with 的程度可能較輕。
Formal; to make progress or movement slower or more difficult.
較正式；使進展或行動變慢或變困難。
Used for getting involved in other people's affairs, always disapproving; interfere can be neutral.
指插手別人的事，帶有負面意味；interfere 可以是中性的。
Interrupt stops a person or activity briefly; interfere with gets in the way of progress or results.
interrupt 是讓人或活動暫時中止；interfere with 是妨礙進展或結果。
To step in on purpose to change a situation, often to help; interfere suggests unwanted involvement.
刻意介入以改變局面，常是為了協助；interfere 則暗示不受歡迎的介入。

def: To stop a person from speaking or an activity from continuing, usually for a short time.
讓人停止說話或讓活動暫停，通常是短暫的。
ex: Sorry to interrupt, but your two o'clock client has arrived.
抱歉打斷一下，你兩點的客戶到了。
A power cut interrupted production at the plant for three hours.
停電使工廠的生產中斷了三個小時。
Please do not interrupt the speaker until the question period begins.
在提問時間開始前，請不要打斷講者。
Frequent phone calls interrupted her work all afternoon.
頻繁的電話整個下午都打斷她的工作。
A fire drill interrupted the training session just after lunch.
午餐剛過，一場消防演習就打斷了訓練課程。

note: Causes serious disorder in a system or event; interrupt only stops it for a time.
造成系統或活動嚴重混亂；interrupt 只是讓它暫時停下來。
Informal phrasal verb for breaking into someone's speech; interrupt is more neutral.
口語的片語動詞，指插嘴；interrupt 較中性。
To disturb is to bother someone who is resting or concentrating; to interrupt is to stop what they are doing.
disturb 是打擾正在休息或專心的人；interrupt 是讓對方停下手邊的事。
Interfere with gets in the way of progress over time; interrupt stops something briefly.
interfere with 是持續妨礙進展；interrupt 是讓事情短暫停止。

def: Machines considered as a group, or the moving parts of a machine.
機器的總稱，或機器的運轉部件。
ex: The factory invested in new machinery to double its output.
工廠投資購買新機器，以使產量加倍。
Workers must wear ear protection near heavy machinery.
在重型機械附近，工作人員必須戴護耳裝置。
The company sells farm machinery to customers across Southeast Asia.
這家公司把農業機械賣給東南亞各地的客戶。
Regular maintenance keeps the packaging machinery running smoothly.
定期保養讓包裝機械運轉順暢。
The machinery of local government can be slow to approve new permits.
地方政府的行政機制在核發新許可時可能很慢。

note: Any tools or gear for a job; machinery means machines with moving parts.
工作所需的任何工具或裝備；machinery 指有運轉部件的機器。
Machine is countable (two machines); machinery is uncountable and never takes an -s.
machine 可數（two machines）；machinery 不可數，不加 -s。

def: To give someone a wrong idea or impression, on purpose or by accident.
有意或無意地讓人產生錯誤的想法或印象。
ex: The advertisement misled customers by hiding the extra fees.
這則廣告隱瞞額外費用，誤導了顧客。
Please don't be misled by the low price; the maintenance costs are high.
請不要被低價誤導；維護成本很高。
The chart misled investors by cutting off the vertical axis.
這張圖表截掉了縱軸，誤導了投資人。
I did not intend to mislead you about the delivery date.
我並非有意誤導你交貨日期。
The company was fined for misleading consumers about where the product was made.
該公司因誤導消費者產品的產地而被罰款。

note: Implies lying or trickery on purpose; mislead can be accidental.
暗示蓄意說謊或欺騙；mislead 可能是無意的。
To give someone wrong facts; mislead stresses that the person ends up with a wrong conclusion.
指提供錯誤的事實；mislead 強調對方因此得出錯誤的結論。

def: To put something somewhere and then be unable to find it.
把東西放在某處後卻找不到。
ex: I seem to have misplaced the key to the supply closet.
我好像把儲藏室的鑰匙放到不知哪裡去了。
Someone misplaced the signed contract, so we asked the client for another copy.
有人把簽好的合約放不見了，所以我們向客戶要了另一份。
The airline misplaced my luggage and promised to deliver it to the hotel.
航空公司弄丟了我的行李，並承諾送到飯店。
If you misplace your security badge, report it to the front desk.
如果你的安全識別證找不到了，請向櫃檯回報。
She misplaced a decimal point in the budget, so the total was ten times too high.
她把預算裡的小數點放錯位置，結果總額高了十倍。

note: Lose is the general word and may be permanent; misplace suggests you expect to find the item again.
lose 是通用字，可能是永遠遺失；misplace 暗示你預期還能找到。
Nearly the same meaning; mislay is a little more formal and old-fashioned, and misplace is the usual choice.
意思幾乎相同；mislay 稍嫌正式老派，一般多用 misplace。
To displace is to force something out of its usual place or take its position; to misplace is to lose track of it.
displace 是迫使某物離開原位或取代其位置；misplace 是放著卻找不到。

zh: 入住率、使用率；佔用、居住
def: The use of a room or building, or the number of rooms or people using it.
對房間或建築物的使用，或使用中的房間數、人數。
ex: The hotel reported ninety percent occupancy during the conference week.
這家飯店回報會議週期間的住房率達九成。
The fire code limits occupancy of this hall to two hundred people.
消防法規限制這座大廳最多容納兩百人。
New tenants may take occupancy of the apartment on the first of the month.
新房客可於當月一日搬入公寓。
Office occupancy has fallen since more staff began working from home.
自從更多員工開始在家工作，辦公室的使用率就下降了。
The quoted rate is based on double occupancy.
報價是以兩人入住一間房計算。

note: Tenancy means renting under an agreement; occupancy simply means using the space, paid or not.
tenancy 指依租約承租；occupancy 只是使用空間，不論是否付費。
An occupant is the person in the space; occupancy is the state or rate of the space being used.
occupant 是使用空間的人；occupancy 是空間被使用的狀態或比率。
Occupation usually means a person's job; occupancy is about using a room or building.
occupation 通常指職業；occupancy 與使用房間或建築物有關。

zh: 居住者、使用者、佔用者；乘員
def: A person who lives in or uses a building, room or vehicle.
居住或使用某棟建築、房間或車輛的人。
ex: The previous occupant of the office left several boxes in the storage room.
這間辦公室的前一位使用者在儲藏室留下了幾個箱子。
Each occupant of the building received a notice about the water shutoff.
大樓的每位住戶都收到停水通知。
All occupants of the vehicle must wear seat belts.
車內所有乘員都必須繫安全帶。
The lease names Ms. Chen as the sole occupant of the apartment.
租約載明陳小姐是這間公寓唯一的住戶。
The sprinklers protect the occupants if a fire breaks out on the third floor.
若三樓發生火災，自動灑水系統會保護裡面的人。

note: A tenant pays rent; an occupant can be anyone in the space, including an owner or a guest.
tenant 付租金；occupant 可以是空間內的任何人，包括屋主或訪客。
Suggests someone who lives in a place for a long time; occupant is neutral and also covers offices and cars.
指長期居住在某地的人；occupant 較中性，也適用於辦公室與車輛。
Occupation usually means a job or the act of taking control; occupant is always a person.
occupation 通常指職業或佔領行為；occupant 一定是指人。

def: A person's job; also the act of entering and holding a place.
一個人的工作；也指進入並控制某地的行為。
ex: Please write your name, address and occupation in the boxes below.
請在下方欄位填寫姓名、地址與職業。
It is common for people to change occupation more than once in their careers.
人們在職涯中不只一次轉換職業是很常見的。
The union ended its occupation of the factory after talks began.
談判開始後，工會結束了對工廠的佔據。
Gardening is her favorite weekend occupation.
園藝是她週末最愛做的事。
Many occupations now require basic data skills.
現在許多職業都需要基本的資料處理能力。

note: A profession needs special training, such as law or medicine; occupation covers any kind of job.
profession 需要專業訓練，如法律或醫學；occupation 涵蓋任何工作。
The everyday word for a specific piece of work; occupation is more formal and common on forms.
指某項具體工作的日常用語；occupation 較正式，常見於表格。
A position is a particular post in a company; an occupation is the general type of work a person does.
position 是公司中的某個職位；occupation 是一個人從事的工作類別。

zh: 多收費、索價過高；多收的款項
def: To ask for more money than the correct or fair price.
索取高於正確或合理價格的金額。
ex: The garage overcharged me for repairs that were never done.
修車廠向我收了根本沒做的維修費。
Customers complained that the taxi driver had overcharged them for the airport trip.
顧客抱怨計程車司機去機場多收了他們的車資。
If you think you were overcharged, send us your receipt and we will check.
如果你認為被多收費了，請把收據寄給我們，我們會查證。
The bank apologized and refunded the overcharge to my account.
銀行道歉，並把多收的款項退回我的帳戶。
Some hotels overcharge guests for minibar items they did not use.
有些飯店對住客沒用過的小冰箱商品也收費。

note: Informal; to charge unfairly high prices, especially when buyers have no choice; overcharge can be a simple mistake.
口語；指趁買方別無選擇而漫天喊價；overcharge 也可能只是失誤。
Informal phrasal verb for cheating someone on price; overcharge is neutral and fits formal complaints.
口語片語，指在價格上坑人；overcharge 較中性，適用於正式申訴。
The seller overcharges; the buyer overpays. They describe the same extra money from opposite sides.
賣方是 overcharge，買方是 overpay；兩者從相反立場描述同一筆多出的錢。

zh: 多付、付過高的薪資或款項
def: To pay someone more than the correct or fair amount.
付給對方超過正確或合理的金額。
ex: We overpaid the supplier by two hundred dollars last month.
我們上個月多付了供應商兩百美元。
If payroll overpays you, the extra amount will be deducted from your next paycheck.
如果薪資部門多發給你錢，多出的金額會從你下次薪水中扣除。
Don't overpay for printer ink; compare prices online first.
別花冤枉錢買印表機墨水，先上網比價。
Several employees were overpaid because of an error in the timesheet system.
由於工時系統出錯，有幾位員工被多發了薪水。
Shareholders argued that the board had overpaid its executives.
股東主張董事會給高階主管的薪酬過高。

note: The buyer overpays; the seller overcharges. Overcharge describes what the seller does.
買方是 overpay；賣方是 overcharge，後者描述賣方的行為。

def: An official document that proves your identity and nationality and lets you travel abroad.
證明身分與國籍、讓你出國旅行的官方文件。
ex: Please bring your passport to the check-in counter for international flights.
搭乘國際航班請攜帶護照到報到櫃檯。
My passport expires in March, so I need to renew it before the business trip.
我的護照三月到期，所以出差前必須先換新。
The border officer stamped her passport and let her through.
邊境人員在她的護照上蓋章後放行。
Make a photocopy of your passport in case it is lost while you travel.
請影印一份護照，以免旅途中遺失。
A good degree can be a passport to a better job.
好的學歷可以是通往更好工作的敲門磚。

note: A visa is permission from a country to enter or stay; a passport is your identity document from your own country.
visa 是他國准許入境或停留的許可；passport 是你本國核發的身分文件。

def: A legal right to be the only person who makes or sells a new invention.
獨家製造或銷售某項新發明的法定權利。
ex: The engineer filed a patent for a more efficient battery design.
這位工程師為一種更有效率的電池設計申請了專利。
The company holds more than forty patents in water filtration.
這家公司擁有四十多項水過濾方面的專利。
Our rival has patented the technology, so we must find another method.
競爭對手已為這項技術取得專利，所以我們必須另找方法。
The patent expires next year, and other firms can then make similar devices.
專利明年到期，屆時其他公司就能製造類似的裝置。
The box is marked patent pending while the application is reviewed.
申請審查期間，盒子上標示著專利申請中。

note: Copyright protects original writing, art, music or code; a patent protects an invention.
copyright 保護原創的文字、藝術、音樂或程式碼；patent 保護發明。
A trademark protects a name or symbol that identifies a business; a patent protects how something works.
trademark 保護識別企業的名稱或標誌；patent 保護事物的運作方式。

def: An animal kept at home for company; also used to mean favorite, as in pet project.
養在家裡作伴的動物；也可表示「特別喜愛的」，如 pet project。
ex: Guests may bring one small pet if they pay a cleaning fee.
住客若支付清潔費，可以攜帶一隻小型寵物。
The apartment building does not allow pets heavier than twenty pounds.
這棟公寓不允許超過二十磅的寵物。
The company has a pet-friendly office, and dogs are welcome on Fridays.
這家公司的辦公室對寵物友善，週五歡迎帶狗上班。
Redesigning the logo has been the director's pet project for years.
重新設計標誌多年來一直是這位主任的心頭好。
Our new pet food line sold out within the first week.
我們新推出的寵物食品系列第一週就賣光了。

note: A pest is an insect or animal that damages crops or property; a pet is an animal kept for company.
pest 是破壞作物或財物的蟲或動物；pet 是養來作伴的動物。

zh: 差地、不好地；（成績、銷量）不佳
def: In a bad way, or at a low standard.
以不好的方式，或在低水準上。
ex: The new product sold poorly because the price was too high.
新產品賣得不好，因為定價太高。
The conference was poorly organized, and many sessions started late.
這場研討會籌辦得不好，許多場次都延遲開始。
Employees who are poorly trained are more likely to make mistakes.
訓練不足的員工比較容易出錯。
The software performed poorly when more than fifty users logged in.
超過五十名使用者登入時，軟體的表現很差。
Entry-level staff are often poorly paid compared with experienced colleagues.
與資深同事相比，初階員工的薪水通常偏低。
Sales did poorly in the first quarter, but the numbers improved by June.
第一季銷售表現不佳，但到六月數字已有起色。

note: The general adverb; poorly stresses low quality or performance, especially before past participles like poorly made.
一般副詞；poorly 強調品質或表現低落，尤其常放在 poorly made 這類過去分詞前。
More formal; means not enough for what is needed, not just low quality.
較正式；指不足以滿足需求，而不只是品質差。

def: To come or happen before something else in time, order or position.
在時間、順序或位置上先於另一事物。
ex: A short safety briefing will precede the factory tour.
工廠參觀之前會先有一場簡短的安全說明。
The CEO's speech was preceded by a video about the company's history.
執行長演講之前先播放了一段公司歷史的影片。
Sales fell in the quarter that preceded the product launch.
產品上市前的那一季，銷售量下滑。
The chapter that precedes this one explains how to set up an account.
本章之前的那一章說明如何建立帳號。
A series of complaints preceded the manager's resignation.
經理辭職之前，先有一連串的客訴。

note: Plain everyday phrase; precede is more formal and common in writing.
平實的日常說法；precede 較正式，常見於書面。
To exist or happen at an earlier date than something else; usually about events or things in the past.
存在或發生的時間早於另一事物；通常指過去的事件或事物。
Proceed means to continue or go ahead; precede means to come before something.
proceed 指繼續進行；precede 指在某事之前。

def: Likely to become something, or likely to happen, in the future.
未來可能成為某種身分，或可能發生的。
ex: We are meeting two prospective clients in Taipei this afternoon.
我們今天下午要在台北跟兩位潛在客戶會面。
The agent showed the prospective tenants around the apartment.
仲介帶準房客參觀這間公寓。
Prospective buyers can view the property on Saturday between ten and four.
有意購買者可於週六十點到四點間看屋。
Please send our prospective suppliers a copy of the quality standards.
請把品質標準的副本寄給我們的潛在供應商。
She is a prospective candidate for the regional manager position.
她是區域經理一職的可能人選。

note: The more common everyday word; prospective points to a person or thing expected to fill a role soon.
較常見的日常用語；prospective 指預期不久會擔任某角色的人或事物。
Only refers to time; prospective suggests someone is likely to take part, such as a buyer or tenant.
只指時間；prospective 暗示某人可能參與，如買家或房客。
Perspective is a point of view; prospective means likely or expected in the future.
perspective 是觀點；prospective 是未來可能的、預期的。

def: The process of finding and hiring new employees.
尋找並聘用新員工的過程。
ex: The company has launched a recruitment drive to fill twenty positions.
公司已展開徵才活動，要補足二十個職缺。
Our recruitment team attends three job fairs every year.
我們的招募團隊每年參加三場就業博覽會。
Recruitment costs rise when a role stays vacant for months.
職缺空了好幾個月時，招募成本就會上升。
She works in recruitment, matching engineers with software companies.
她從事人力招募，替軟體公司媒合工程師。
The recruitment of skilled technicians has become difficult in this region.
在這個地區，招募熟練技師已變得困難。

note: Plainer word focused on the act of employing someone; recruitment covers searching for and attracting candidates too.
較平實，著重聘僱的動作；recruitment 還包含尋找與吸引人選。
Broader: making sure a business has enough workers, including scheduling; recruitment is only finding new people.
範圍較廣：確保企業有足夠人力，包括排班；recruitment 只指尋找新人。

def: The act of gaining control of a company or organization.
取得公司或組織控制權的行為。
ex: Shareholders approved the takeover after the board raised its offer.
董事會提高報價後，股東核准了這項收購案。
The bank announced a hostile takeover bid for its smaller rival.
這家銀行宣布對規模較小的對手展開敵意收購。
After the takeover, the new owners reorganized the sales department.
收購完成後，新東家重整了業務部門。
Employees feared job losses when news of the takeover spread.
收購消息傳開時，員工擔心會失業。
The sudden takeover of the project by head office surprised the local team.
總公司突然接管這項專案，讓當地團隊相當意外。

note: Neutral word for buying a company or asset; takeover stresses gaining control, sometimes against the owners' wishes.
購買公司或資產的中性用語；takeover 強調取得控制權，有時違背原所有人意願。
The purchase of all or most shares of a company, often by managers or investors.
買下公司全部或大部分股份，常由經理人或投資人進行。
A merger joins two companies, usually as partners; in a takeover one company takes control of the other.
merger 是兩家公司合併，通常是對等夥伴；takeover 是一家公司取得另一家的控制權。

def: A name, symbol or design that a company registers to identify its products.
公司登記用來識別其產品的名稱、符號或圖案。
ex: The company registered the name as a trademark before launching the product.
公司在推出產品之前，先把這個名稱註冊為商標。
Using another firm's trademark without permission can lead to a lawsuit.
未經許可使用他家公司的商標可能會引來訴訟。
The bakery trademarked its logo to stop imitations.
這家麵包店為了防止仿冒而註冊了自己的標誌。
A registered trademark is marked with the symbol ®.
已註冊的商標會標上 ® 符號。
Careful planning is the trademark of a good project manager.
周詳的規劃是優秀專案經理的招牌特色。

note: The name and image customers know; a trademark is the legal protection of that name or symbol.
顧客熟悉的名稱與形象；trademark 是對該名稱或標誌的法律保護。
A logo is a visual design; a trademark can be a name, slogan or logo that is registered by law.
logo 是視覺圖樣；trademark 可以是依法註冊的名稱、標語或標誌。
A patent protects an invention; a trademark protects a name or symbol that identifies a business.
patent 保護發明；trademark 保護識別企業的名稱或標誌。
Copyright protects creative works such as books and music, not brand names.
copyright 保護書籍、音樂等創作，不保護品牌名稱。

def: A person who is making a journey, especially to a distant place.
正在旅行的人，尤指前往遠方的人。
ex: Business travelers often prefer hotels near the airport.
商務旅客常偏好機場附近的飯店。
The airline offers a special lounge for frequent travelers.
這家航空公司為常客提供專屬貴賓室。
Each traveler must show a boarding pass at the security gate.
每位旅客都必須在安檢口出示登機證。
Experienced travelers pack light to avoid baggage fees.
經驗豐富的旅客會輕裝簡行，以避免行李費。
The tourism board surveyed international travelers about their hotel experiences.
觀光局針對國際旅客的住宿體驗做了問卷調查。

note: A passenger rides in a vehicle such as a plane or train; a traveler is anyone on a journey.
passenger 是搭乘飛機、火車等交通工具的人；traveler 是任何在旅途中的人。
A tourist travels for pleasure; a traveler may travel for business or other reasons.
tourist 為遊玩而旅行；traveler 可能是為了商務或其他原因。
A commuter makes regular trips between home and work; a traveler goes on a journey, often to somewhere far.
commuter 是定期往返住處與工作地點的人；traveler 是出遠門的人。

zh: 營業額；人員流動率；週轉率
def: The amount of business a company does, or the rate at which employees leave and are replaced.
公司的營業量，或員工離開並被替補的比率。
ex: High staff turnover is expensive because every new hire must be trained.
員工流動率高會很花錢，因為每位新進人員都要訓練。
The company reported an annual turnover of twelve million dollars.
該公司公布年營業額為一千兩百萬美元。
Inventory turnover improved after we cut the number of slow-moving items.
我們減少滯銷品項後，存貨週轉率改善了。
The restaurant's quick table turnover keeps waiting times short.
這間餐廳翻桌速度快，所以候位時間短。
A new bonus scheme helped cut employee turnover by fifteen percent.
新的獎金制度幫助把員工離職率降低了百分之十五。

note: The standard American term for income from sales; turnover with this meaning is mostly British.
美式標準用語，指銷售收入；turnover 作此義多為英式用法。
Gradual loss of staff, often without replacement; turnover counts people who leave and are replaced.
指員工逐漸流失，常不補人；turnover 計算離職並被補上的人數。
Turnaround is the time taken to complete a task, or a sudden improvement; turnover is staff change or sales volume.
turnaround 指完成工作所需時間或情勢好轉；turnover 指人員更替或營業量。

def: Needing immediate action or attention.
需要立即處理或注意。
ex: I have an urgent message for Ms. Lee from the head office.
我有一則總公司要給李小姐的緊急訊息。
The client sent an urgent request for a revised quotation.
客戶緊急要求提供修改後的報價單。
Repairs to the roof are urgent because the leaks are getting worse.
屋頂的修繕刻不容緩，因為漏水愈來愈嚴重。
It is urgent that we confirm the venue by Friday.
我們必須在週五前確認場地，事不宜遲。
There is an urgent need for more nurses at the clinic.
這家診所迫切需要更多護理師。

note: A bit more formal; usually describes problems or needs that must be dealt with now.
稍微正式；通常用來形容必須立即處理的問題或需求。
Stresses very serious consequences if nothing is done; urgent stresses lack of time.
強調不處理會有非常嚴重的後果；urgent 強調時間緊迫。
Important matters count for a lot but may not need action now; urgent matters cannot wait.
重要的事影響很大，但不一定要馬上處理；緊急的事則不能等。
Emergency is a noun for a sudden dangerous situation; urgent describes anything that needs quick action.
emergency 是名詞，指突發的危急狀況；urgent 形容任何需要快速處理的事。

def: To leave a room, building, seat or job so that others can use it.
離開房間、建築、座位或職位，讓別人可以使用。
ex: Guests must vacate their rooms by eleven a.m. on the day of departure.
住客必須在離開當天上午十一點前退房。
The tenant agreed to vacate the apartment at the end of the lease.
房客同意租約結束時搬離公寓。
Please vacate the meeting room; another team has booked it for ten o'clock.
請把會議室讓出來；另一個團隊預約了十點使用。
The director will vacate her post in June, and the search for a successor has begun.
主任六月將卸任，接班人的遴選已經展開。
Residents were asked to vacate the premises while workers removed the asbestos.
工人清除石綿期間，住戶被要求離開該處。

note: Everyday word; vacate is formal and stresses emptying a place for the next user.
日常用語；vacate 較正式，強調把地方空出來給下一位使用者。
Informal; used for homes and offices when you stop living or working there.
口語；用於不再住在或使用某住處、辦公室時。
To evacuate is to move people out because of danger; to vacate is simply to leave a place you were using.
evacuate 是因危險而讓人撤離；vacate 只是離開原本使用的地方。

zh: 有效的；合理的、站得住腳的
def: Legally acceptable or still usable; based on good reasons.
在法律上被接受或仍可使用；有充分理由支持。
ex: You need a valid ticket to enter the exhibition hall.
你需要有效的門票才能進入展覽館。
This coupon is valid until the end of the month.
這張優惠券在月底前有效。
She raised a valid point about the delivery costs.
她對運費提出了一個合理的看法。
The contract is only valid if both parties sign it.
這份合約必須雙方都簽名才有效。
Please show a valid photo ID at the reception desk.
請在接待櫃檯出示有效的附照片證件。

note: Allowed by law or reasonable and genuine; often used for businesses, claims and reasons.
合法，或合理且真實；常用於企業、主張與理由。
Only means allowed by law; valid can also describe tickets, arguments and points.
只表示法律允許；valid 也能形容票券、論點與看法。
Available means able to be obtained or used right now; valid means officially accepted or not yet expired.
available 指現在可取得或使用；valid 指被正式認可或尚未過期。
